title: BRICKSTORM_Backdoor_Investigation_324
description: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a potential BRICKSTORM backdoor infection on your organization's Linux systems. The backdoor uses sophisticated techniques including SOCKS proxying, multi-layered web service communication, and varied command execution to obscure its activities. Your mission is to identify, contain, and eradicate this threat.
outcomes: Identify and investigate suspicious services and processes
Analyze network communications for command-and-control activity

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a potential BRICKSTORM backdoor infection on your organization's Linux systems. The backdoor uses sophisticated techniques including SOCKS proxying, multi-layered web service communication, and varied command execution to obscure its activities. Your mission is to identify, contain, and eradicate this threat.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Connect to the target host using the provided credentials via SSH. Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano! Enter 'start' to begin.
levels.local_content: Connect to the target host using the provided credentials via SSH. Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano! Enter 'start' to begin.

levels.title: Suspicious Service Discovery
levels.content: While monitoring system logs on the target host, you noticed unusual network activity. Investigate the running services on this host to identify any unauthorized or suspicious services. Submit the name of the suspicious service.
levels.solution:
1. Connect to the target host using the provided credentials
2. Enumerate all running services and processes
3. Identify any services or processes that appear suspicious or unauthorized
4. Document your findings, including the service name, process ID, and any relevant details
5. The suspicious service name is brickstorm.service

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Look for services that don't match the expected software inventory for this system. Pay attention to unusual process names, high network usage, or services listening on unexpected ports.

levels.title: C2 Communication Discovery
levels.content: You've identified a suspicious service on the target host. Now investigate its network communications to determine if it's connecting to a command-and-control server. Submit the port number used for this communication.
levels.solution:
1. Analyze the network connections associated with the suspicious service
2. Identify any external IP addresses or domains it's communicating with
3. Determine the network ports being used for this communication
4. Document your findings, including the destination IP, port, and any patterns in the communication
5. The port number used for C2 communication is 443

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use network monitoring tools to capture and analyze the traffic. Look for unusual connection patterns, such as regular check-ins or data exfiltration.

levels.title: Lateral Movement Investigation
levels.content: You suspect the BRICKSTORM backdoor might be attempting to move laterally within your network. Investigate the target host for any signs of lateral movement to other systems. Submit the name of the service involved in lateral movement.
levels.solution:
1. Examine the target host for any evidence of file transfers or remote command execution
2. Check for any established connections to other hosts in the network
3. Investigate system logs for any unauthorized access attempts or data transfers
4. Document your findings, including the destination host, transferred files, and any relevant details
5. The service involved in lateral movement is payload-transfer.service

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Look for SSH connections, file transfer utilities, or remote command execution tools. Check system logs for any unusual access patterns or data transfers.
